extracted.title: ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor - Nepal (Recent Developments)
extracted.description: ICNL overview notes that in March 2026 Nepal formed a new government after elections held in the wake of a youth-led protest movement triggered by social media restrictions that collapsed the prior government in September 2025.
extracted.snippet: In March 2026, Nepal formed a new government after elections, which saw the governing coalition secure a nearly two-thirds majority. The 2026 elections were held in the wake of a youth-led protest movement triggered by social media restrictions, which led to the collapse of the prior government in September 2025.

extracted.title: ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor - Nepal (Barriers to Resources)
extracted.description: ICNL reports that associations must obtain case-by-case approval from the Social Welfare Council to receive government or foreign funding, and banks will not release transferred donor funds without an SWC authorization letter.
extracted.snippet: Associations must obtain case-by-case approval from the Social Welfare Council (SWC) to receive government or foreign funding. Even after funds are transferred under an agreement with a bilateral or multilateral donor, banks will not release them without an official SWC authorization letter.

extracted.title: ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor - Nepal (NGO registration numbers)
extracted.description: As of March 2026 the Social Welfare Council's database listed 57,978 active NGOs, while a separate study estimated 25,760 NGOs were active at the end of fiscal year 2024-25; 119 international CSOs were listed as of April 2025.
extracted.snippet: As of March 2026, the Social Welfare Council's database listed 57,978 NGOs as active. A March 2026 study, Counting Nepal's NGOs, presents a different view, estimating that 25,760 NGOs were active at the end of fiscal year 2024–25. The SWC database also listed 119 international CSOs as of April 2025.

extracted.title: ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor - Nepal (draft NGO Registration Bill)
extracted.description: In August 2025 Nepal's Ministry of Home Affairs issued a draft NGO Registration, Regulation and Management Bill that would consolidate the Associations Registration Act (1977), National Directorate Act (1961), and Social Welfare Act (1992).
extracted.snippet: In August 2025, Nepal's Ministry of Home Affairs issued a draft NGO Registration, Regulation and Management Bill, which seeks to consolidate three existing laws governing NGOs in Nepal: the Associations Registration Act (1977), the National Directorate Act (1961), and the Social Welfare Act (1992).

extracted.title: ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor - Nepal (Karki Commission recommendations)
extracted.description: ICNL states that Karki Commission recommendations, including expanded digital monitoring and a specialized social media intelligence unit, could facilitate surveillance of organizers and constrain assembly mobilization.
extracted.snippet: Recommendations of the Karki Commission, including expanded digital monitoring, a specialized social media intelligence unit, and stronger regulation of online platforms, could facilitate surveillance of organizers and further constrain the coordination and mobilization of peaceful assemblies.

extracted.title: ICNL Civic Freedom Monitor - Nepal (assembly right restricted to citizens)
extracted.description: ICNL notes that Nepal's constitutional right to peaceful assembly is restricted to Nepali citizens, contrary to international law standards on freedom of assembly.
extracted.snippet: section (17)(2)(b) of the Constitution of Nepal guarantees that "every citizen shall have … the freedom to assemble peaceably and without arms." This right is restricted to Nepali citizens, in contravention of international law standards on freedom of assembly.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Nepal country rating
extracted.description: CIVICUS Monitor rates Nepal's civic space as 'Obstructed' with a current score of 48/100, and shows the country rated 'obstructed' continuously from 2018 through 2024.
extracted.snippet: Current score | Current rating | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 ... 48 | Obstructed | obstructed | obstructed | obstructed

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Nepal: Civic space at risk (Nov 2024 baseline report)
extracted.description: CIVICUS documented that peaceful protests in Nepal have been met with arbitrary arrests and excessive force including firearms, with unlawful killings reported and no accountability, alongside government limits on protest space.
extracted.snippet: However, in recent years peaceful protests have been met with arbitrary arrests and excessive force, including the use of firearms. In some cases, unlawful killings have been reported, with no one held to account.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Nepal transitional justice law adopted (Aug 2024)
extracted.description: Nepal's transitional justice law was adopted by the lower house of parliament on 14 August 2024, incorporating provisions to advance justice for 1996-2006 conflict-era abuses, though human rights groups raised concerns about shortcomings.
extracted.snippet: Nepal's long-awaited transitional justice law, adopted by the lower house of parliament on 14th August 2024, incorporates many positive provisions that could help in advancing justice, accountability and redress for the widespread human rights violations and abuses committed during the 1996-2006 conflict.

extracted.title: OHCHR - Türk welcomes adoption of Nepal transitional justice law
extracted.description: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk stated that the adoption of new transitional justice legislation in Nepal marks an important step toward accountability and reconciliation, while calling for victim-centred implementation.
extracted.snippet: GENEVA (22 August 2024) – The adoption of new transitional justice legislation in Nepal marks an important step in the nation's long journey towards accountability and reconciliation, UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk said today.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Electronic Transaction Act used against online critics (2024)
extracted.description: CIVICUS documented ongoing persecution of individuals for online criticism of politicians under the Electronic Transaction Act 2008, including arrests of individuals posting Facebook criticism of the Prime Minister and other leaders in August 2024.
extracted.snippet: There are also concerns about online restrictions, especially the use of the Electronic Transactions Act 2008 to stifle dissent... Ramesh Bahadur Rawal... who posted a Facebook status calling Prime Minister Oli as corrupt was arrested on 16th August 2024 and charged with spreading public hatred.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Ruby Khan activists arrested and later reach agreement (2024)
extracted.description: Human rights defender Ruby Khan and fellow activists protesting for justice were repeatedly arrested/detained in Kathmandu in September-October 2024 before suspending their protest following a three-point agreement with the Ministry of Home Affairs on 29 October 2024.
extracted.snippet: On 29th October 2024, the group suspended their protest following a three-point agreement with the Ministry of Home Affairs. The government agreed to expedite the investigation into the abduction, unlawful confinement and murder of Nirmala Kurmi.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Kantipur Media chair Sirohiya arrested (May 2024)
extracted.description: Kailash Sirohiya, chairperson of Kantipur Media Group, was arrested on 21 May 2024 over citizenship document issues; press freedom groups viewed the arrest as retaliation for reporting on the Home Minister.
extracted.snippet: The chairperson and publisher of the Kantipur Media Group, Kailash Sirohiya, was arrested on 21st May 2024, allegedly over supposed irregularities in the details on his citizenship card.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - UN experts on HRD retaliation over Chhaya Center (2024)
extracted.description: UN experts expressed concern on 14 May 2024 over reprisals against human rights defenders opposing the Chhaya Center development in Kathmandu, including intimidation and a contempt of court case against activist Bhagabat Narsingh Pradhan.
extracted.snippet: UN experts expressed concern on 14th May 2024 over reports of ongoing retaliations against human rights defenders because of their opposition to the development of the Chhaya Center retail and entertainment complex in Nepal.

extracted.title: CIVICUS/AHRC Joint UPR51 Submission on Nepal
extracted.description: CIVICUS and the Asian Human Rights Commission's July 2025 UN Universal Periodic Review submission found Nepal has not fully implemented any of 11 accepted civic-space recommendations, with seven unaddressed and six partially fulfilled.
extracted.snippet: Despite accepting 11 out of 13 recommendations, Nepal has not fully implemented any, with seven entirely unaddressed and six only partially fulfilled.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Social Media Bill introduced (Feb 2025)
extracted.description: On 9 February 2025 the 'Bill on the Operation, Use, and Regulation of Social Media' was introduced in Nepal's National Assembly, proposing registration, penalisation, content moderation, and criminal penalties for online speech.
extracted.snippet: On 9th February 2025, the 'Bill on the Operation, Use, and Regulation of Social Media', referred to as the Social Media Act Bill, was introduced in Nepal's National Assembly, designed to regulate social media platforms and users through increased registration, penalisation, and content moderation.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Media Council Bill passed (Feb 2025)
extracted.description: The Media Council Bill, replacing the Press Council with a government-influenced Media Council regulatory body, was passed in February 2025, raising concerns about government control over independent media.
extracted.snippet: Concerns have been raised around a Media Council Bill that was passed in February 2025. The new Media Council Bill replaces the existing Press Council responsible for upholding the standards of free press with the Media Council, a new regulatory body.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - unregistered social media platforms warned (May 2025)
extracted.description: On 9 May 2025 the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology again warned social media platforms to register under the 2023 Directives; major platforms including Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram and X had not complied.
extracted.snippet: On 9th May 2025, Digital Rights Nepal reported that The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology has once again issued a warning to social media platforms to register in Nepal under the Directives for Managing the Use of Social Networks, 2023.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - civil society coalition statement on digital regulation (May 2025)
extracted.description: In early May 2025, Digital Rights Nepal convened a coalition of 31 civil society organisations, digital rights advocates and media groups issuing recommendations for transparent, inclusive digital platform regulation.
extracted.snippet: In early May 2025, Digital Rights Nepal convened a coalition of 31 civil society organisations, digital rights advocates, and media groups. They issued a joint public statement, making a number of recommendations including to ensure that any regulation of digital platforms is transparent, inclusive, and rooted in democratic principles.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - HRW January 2025 report on impunity
extracted.description: Human Rights Watch said in January 2025 that lack of justice for conflict-era crimes has contributed to a widespread crisis of impunity in Nepal, undermining human rights, governance and rule of law.
extracted.snippet: Human Rights Watch (HRW) said in January 2025 that the lack of justice for conflict-era crimes has contributed to a widespread crisis of impunity in Nepal, undermining human rights, governance, and the rule of law.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - ICJ report on transitional justice pledge (March 2025)
extracted.description: In March 2025 the International Commission of Jurists reported that Nepal's political leaders including PM Oli, together with civil society, pledged to redouble efforts on victim-centred transitional justice mechanisms.
extracted.snippet: In March 2025, the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) reported that Nepal's leading political authorities, including the Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, together with civil society groups, have pledged to redouble their efforts to improve and implement effective transitional justice mechanisms.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Amnesty International April 2025 report on 2024 suppression
extracted.description: Amnesty International said in April 2025 that the Nepal government suppressed criticism in 2024 through protest restrictions, unlawful force, and forcible dispersal/detention of demonstrators, with intensified restrictions on journalists and online critics.
extracted.snippet: In April 2025, Amnesty International said that the government suppressed criticism in 2024 by enforcing restrictions on protests, using unlawful force, and forcibly dispersing and detaining demonstrators.

extracted.title: Kathmandu Post - NHRC reform bill in limbo (July 2025)
extracted.description: Nepal's government had yet to finalise a new National Human Rights Commission Act eight months after the draft bill was submitted (Sept 2024), despite the reform being a factor in retaining the NHRC's global 'A' accreditation status.
extracted.snippet: However, eight months down the line, the government has yet to finalise the bill. Officials have no idea when the bill will be finalised and registered in Parliament.

extracted.title: Kathmandu Post - counter-intelligence wing bill (Aug 2025)
extracted.description: A draft bill to replace the Nepal Special Service Act would create a formal counter-intelligence wing empowering the National Investigation Department to collect intelligence and conduct surveillance activities, including on espionage and subversion.
extracted.snippet: The bill lays out legal provisions for surveillance, secret missions, handling informants, evidence collection, interrogation, and verification — all of which are professional counter-intelligence activities.

extracted.title: Khabarhub - lawmaker warns Intelligence Bill threatens privacy (Aug 2025)
extracted.description: Nepali Congress lawmaker NP Saud warned in Parliament that the government's draft Intelligence Bill would allow control, monitoring and tapping of citizens' phone calls and messages, violating constitutional privacy guarantees.
extracted.snippet: Saud said the proposed legislation would allow the government to control, monitor, and tap citizens' phone calls, messages, and other communications, a move he argued goes against the spirit of the constitution.

extracted.title: Kathmandu Post opinion - Nepal's civil society under siege (Aug 2025)
extracted.description: Opinion piece describes the 2025 draft Social Organisation/NGO bill as the third attempt to regulate civil society under PM Oli (after 2016 and 2019), introducing expanded reporting obligations, special-audit powers, and geographic/sectoral restrictions.
extracted.snippet: The 2025 draft marks the third attempt to regulate social organisations under the premiership of KP Sharma Oli, following similar efforts in 2016 and 2019.

extracted.title: Peoples' Review - Government intends to tighten NGOs (Sept 2025)
extracted.description: The Home Ministry unveiled a bill to amend and integrate NGO registration, regulation and management laws, proposing to dissolve the Social Welfare Council; the NGO Federation called the bill 'retrograde and cumbersome.'
extracted.snippet: The bill integrates the National Directives Act (1961), the Association Registration Act (1977), and the Social Welfare Act (1992) and proposes dissolving the Social Welfare Council (SWC) and replacing it with a new social welfare act under the Home Ministry.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - social media ban on 26 platforms (Sept 2025)
extracted.description: On 4 September 2025 the government ordered the Nepal Telecommunications Authority to block 26 unregistered social media platforms, precipitating the Gen Z protests.
extracted.snippet: On 4th September 2025, the government ordered the Nepal Telecommunications Authority to block 26 unregistered social

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - deadly Gen Z protest crackdown (Sept 2025)
extracted.description: Police used lethal force against Gen Z protesters on 8-9 September 2025 following a social media ban, with at least 19 killed on the first day (rising to 76 total nationwide) and hundreds injured; PM Oli resigned and the ban was lifted.
extracted.snippet: Police responded with water cannon, tear gas, rubber bullets and live ammunition, leaving at least nineteen dead and hundreds injured... By 12th September 2025, officials said the number of fatalities caused by two days of violence had reached 51.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - interim government under Sushila Karki formed (Sept 2025)
extracted.description: On 12 September 2025 an agreement was reached to dissolve parliament and swear in former Chief Justice Sushila Karki as interim Prime Minister, the first woman to hold the position, with fresh elections announced for 5 March 2026.
extracted.snippet: an agreement was reached to dissolve parliament and swear in former Chief Justice Sushila Karki - the first woman to hold the position - as head of an interim government that would conduct fresh elections announced for 5th March 2026.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - draft NGO law concerns amid 2025 unrest
extracted.description: CIVICUS noted continued concerns around a social media bill and that a draft NGO law had raised concerns about increasing controls and burdensome requirements for civil society.
extracted.snippet: There are continued concerns around a social media bill and a draft NGO law has raised concerns about increasing controls and burdensome requirements for civil society.

extracted.title: HRW - Unlawful Use of Force During Gen Z Protest (Nov 2025)
extracted.description: Human Rights Watch found that on 8 September 2025 police indiscriminately fired on protesters for over three hours, killing 17 in Kathmandu, with dozens detained and some beaten; violence continued on 9 September including arson attacks.
extracted.snippet: In November 2025, Human Rights Watch (HRW) reported that security forces in Nepal used disproportionate force against youth-led protests in September 2025. HRW found that on 8th September 2025, police indiscriminately fired on protesters multiple times over three hours.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Amnesty International report on unlawful killings (Dec 2025)
extracted.description: Amnesty International's December 2025 briefing found widespread failings by Nepal's law enforcement during the September protests, documenting unlawful killings and excessive/lethal force including live ammunition against largely peaceful protesters.
extracted.snippet: In another report, published in December 2025, Amnesty International said there were widespread failings by Nepal's law enforcement agencies in policing September's protest that resulted in unlawful killings, unnecessary and excessive use of force, and severe injuries.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Nepal UN Human Rights Council review (Jan 2026)
extracted.description: On 21 January 2026 Nepal's human rights record was reviewed at the UN Human Rights Council, with states recommending a safe environment for expression, ensuring the constitutional right to assembly, and accountability for protest-related violence.
extracted.snippet: On 21st January 2026, Nepal's human rights record was reviewed at the UN Human Rights Council where recommendations were made by states... They were also recommended to ensure the constitutional right to peaceful assembly, refrain from excessive use of force by security agencies.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - HRW annual report on Nepal (Feb 2026)
extracted.description: Human Rights Watch's annual report (Feb 2026) highlighted documented police use of excessive and lethal force during 2025 protests and noted that transitional justice progress stalled after victims' groups rejected commissioners as unqualified.
extracted.snippet: On 4th February 2026, Human Rights Watch issued its annual report and highlighted that in 2025 they documented police use of excessive and lethal force during protests... progress on justice for human rights violations committed during the 1996-2006 conflict stalled after victims' groups rejected the commissioners appointed to the transitional justice bodies.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Karki Commission of inquiry term extended (Jan-Feb 2026)
extracted.description: The judicial commission of inquiry chaired by Gauri Bahadur Karki, investigating 76 protest-related deaths, had its term extended by Cabinet on 22 January 2026 and again on 9 February 2026, partly over fears its findings could disrupt the election.
extracted.snippet: On 9th February 2026 its deadline was extended for another 25 days beyond election day, for fear that its findings could be opposed by security forces or political actors and cause "friction" in the election environment.

extracted.title: Kathmandu Post / Eu SEE - Social Media Bill formally withdrawn (Feb 2026)
extracted.description: The Karki-led interim government moved on 3-6 February 2026 to withdraw the controversial 2025 Social Media Bill from the National Assembly amid sustained civil society criticism that its provisions were overly broad.
extracted.snippet: The government of Nepal has moved to withdraw the controversial Social Media Bill from the National Assembly. The decision, taken on 6 February 2026, by the government, reverses a proposal introduced by the previous government in February 2025.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - RSP wins general election (March 2026)
extracted.description: On 5 March 2026 the Rastriya Swatantra Party led by Balendra Shah won a clear majority (182 of 275 seats) in Nepal's snap general election held six months after the September 2025 protests toppled the government.
extracted.snippet: On 5th March 2026, the party of rapper and ex-Kathmandu mayor Balendra Shah won a clear majority, in the general election. The Rastriya Swatantra Party's (RSP) victory marks the first time in decades that a single party has garnered a majority in Nepal.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - former PM Oli and Home Minister arrested (March 2026)
extracted.description: Following Balendra Shah's swearing-in as PM on 27 March 2026, former PM K.P. Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak were arrested over the deadly police crackdown on the September 2025 protests, per commission recommendations.
extracted.snippet: In a strong first move by the new government, former prime minister K.P. Sharma Oli was arrested the day after Shah's swearing-in ceremony, following recommendations from a commission set up to investigate the deadly police crackdown on protests in September 2025. Former home minister Ramesh Lekhak was also arrested.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - Karki Commission report findings (March 2026)
extracted.description: The Karki Commission's report, submitted 8 March 2026, confirmed 76 deaths (42 from police firing) and recommended criminal proceedings against ex-PM Oli, Home Minister Lekhak, and IGP Khapung for negligence, plus victim compensation and police reforms.
extracted.snippet: The report confirms 76 deaths: 42 from police firing (mostly protesters), 3 police killed by mobs, and the rest during looting. It recommended criminal proceedings against then-Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak, and IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung for negligence leading to deaths.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - NHRC recommendations on protest investigation (May 2026)
extracted.description: On 27 May 2026 Nepal's National Human Rights Commission publicised recommendations including investigating Karki Commission chair for social media posts, and probing 17 sitting RSP MPs regarding the September 2025 unrest.
extracted.snippet: On 27th May 2026, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of Nepal publicised recommendations it has provided to the Nepal government in relation to the protests... It recommended that the government undertake detailed investigations on the role of several individuals, including 17 sitting members of parliament representing the governing RSP.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - press freedom concerns in first 100 days of new government (2026)
extracted.description: Media observers reported mounting pressure on press freedom in PM Balendra Shah's first 100 days, including a June 2026 statement by Home Minister Sudan Gurung that the Home Ministry would act against media outlets deemed to insult or defame individuals.
extracted.snippet: Home Minister Sudan Gurung in June 2026 said that the Home Ministry would take action against media organisations that insult or defame individuals. This is despite under Nepal's existing legal framework, complaints against the media fall under the jurisdiction of the Press Council Nepal.

extracted.title: CIVICUS Monitor - journalist assaulted covering election campaign (Feb 2026)
extracted.description: Journalist Arjun Acharya was assaulted on 26 February 2026 while covering K.P. Sharma Oli's election campaign activities in Jhapa district, allegedly by individuals associated with CPN-UML's volunteer force.
extracted.snippet: Ahead of the federal elections, Arjun Acharya, a reporter with RatoPati.com and an executive editor of Hamromat.com was assaulted. This occurred on 26 February (February 26), while covering the election activities of K. P. Sharma Oli.

extracted.title: Kathmandu Post - NHRC reform status review (March 2025)
extracted.description: Nepal's National Human Rights Commission underwent a periodic accreditation review in March 2025; the commission had drafted a new Act in line with the Paris Principles and forwarded it to the PMO on 3 September 2024, but the government had yet to finalise it.
extracted.snippet: Although the commission on September 3, 2024 submitted a draft bill for its new Act to the Prime Minister's Office (PMO), the government has yet to finalise it. The bill is under evaluation at the Ministry of Finance.

extracted.title: Kathmandu Post - Nepal's UN human rights report questioned (Dec 2025)
extracted.description: Nepal presented a report to the UN claiming progress on NHRC autonomy and a draft NHRC Act aligned with the Paris Principles, but human rights advocates said the claims presented before the UPR were exaggerated.
extracted.snippet: The report claims that a new bill of the NHRC Act has been drafted in line with Nepal's constitution and the Paris Principles... However, the claims in the report presented before the United Nations are exaggerated, say those working in human rights advocacy.
